evidence_gaps.close_condition: Every sound-dependent claim is either supported by direct audition or removed before an evidence-backed final disposition.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Directly audition the existing local Sound of Metal intervals and record exact audible state observations.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate reaches one of the five final states only after a single exact source-to-change-to-result chain is verified in moving image; a new positive rule also needs unrelated same-trigger support and a real boundary.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Select and replay one complete adjacent micro-action chain per work, including source, target before-state, visible change, result, and response; do not combine unrelated action fragments or infer cross-cut identity and causality.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each route-anchor candidate is either bound to a shared state-changing threshold trigger with one same-trigger boundary, merged into DR-STATE-CHANGING-THRESHOLD-CHECKPOINT, or rejected because the reviewed motion shows only travel continuity without a distinct directing decision.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the full entry, checkpoint, interruption, and exit intervals for all 13 candidates; distinguish a story-state-changing threshold from ordinary route coverage, then locate a same-trigger non-use case inside the closed corpus.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate is classified as a comparative-field decision, a visible custody/state-change decision, a continuity-only constraint, a duplicate, or an evidence-backed rejection; any new positive has two works and a same-trigger boundary.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the object reveal, handoff, update, and return intervals for all 12 candidates; record who can see or control the object before and after each cut, and separate active shot/edit choices from passive prop continuity.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate is either fresh support for a named reset rule, a distinct positive rule with cross-work support and a same-trigger boundary, a duplicate, or rejected because no spatial change alters coverage or blocking.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the complete pre-change, change, and post-change motion for all 10 candidates; mark the last stable geometry and first usable reset, and distinguish material relation changes from stable-axis coverage that needs no reset.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate has a verified information/event receiver, an observable reaction-distribution choice, and a same-trigger boundary, or is merged/rejected when the image only shows generic singles without receiver priority.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the trigger and every proposed receiver interval for all 12 candidates; directly audition or bind a short text anchor whenever the triggering information is not visible, then compare event/receiver ordering across unrelated works.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Every candidate has continuous moving-image evidence for duration, occlusion, route reacquisition, and visible cut points; each is then promoted with a same-trigger boundary, merged, or rejected as a descriptive long-take label.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Inspect each proposed continuous passage in motion from entry through exit, including suspected hidden joins and occlusions; verify whether continuity itself carries story evidence and find a same-trigger case where segmentation is preferable.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate identifies a visibly completed event, the first stable aftermath state, and a director decision that differs from ordinary scene closure; otherwise it is merged or rejected, and any positive has a same-trigger boundary.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the decisive event through the proposed recovery or exit for all five candidates; establish whether the event is actually terminal at that point and whether the hold, distribution, or exit verification changes coverage, pacing, or edit.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate has a shot-by-shot before/after ledger tied to a visible version or state change that changes coverage, blocking, or edit; continuity-only reminders without a directing delta receive REJECTED_WITH_REASON.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay every visible handoff, version change, body/surface change, and return for the five candidates; record the exact shot where the state changes and the exact later shot whose director choice depends on remembering it.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each workflow candidate has verified step order, actor/receiver handoff, and a shot/edit consequence; audio- or text-dependent semantics are directly established, otherwise the candidate is merged or rejected rather than promoted.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the full task sequence for all five candidates and directly audition or bind short text anchors where step order, authority, hypothesis, or handoff meaning is not visible; compare only genuinely equivalent workflow triggers.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Both remaining candidates are either merged into a reviewed relation-geometry rule, used as a verified same-trigger boundary, or rejected because room registration/decompression does not change a distinct director decision.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the complete approach, closest relation point, separation, singles, and room reset for the two remaining candidates; test whether they add a distinct trigger or are only neighboring phases of DR-SHARED-FRAME-FOR-RELATION-ENDPOINT.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate has verified concurrent story threads, visible or directly established state changes in each thread, and a specific intercut/merge point; otherwise it is merged or rejected rather than treated as generic cross-cutting.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay all four proposed thread structures from first split through recombination; directly audition or bind text where thread goals are not visible, and verify that cut order follows state change rather than chronology alone.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate has a measurable detail-to-container or scale progression that changes coverage/pacing, plus a same-trigger case where that ladder should not be used; descriptive shot-size variation alone is rejected.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the four proposed scale/reveal sequences in motion, record the information disclosed at each scale change, and distinguish deliberate reveal order from ordinary shot-size coverage before seeking cross-work support.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each remaining candidate is either fresh support/boundary for DR-PERFORMANCE-OWNER-HOLD or rejected as generic subject coverage; no new rule is allowed without a distinct trigger and same-trigger boundary.
evidence_gaps.required_review: Replay the full ownership transfer around the two remaining candidates; establish who owns the decisive performance beat, whether a counterpart stays visible, and whether the hold changes reaction or edit timing.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Each candidate has a verified before-state, visible event, after-state, and exact cut/hold decision; sound-linked timing is directly auditioned, and any promoted rule has a same-trigger boundary rather than merely a temporal sequence.

evidence_gaps.close_condition: Both candidates demonstrate that a stable axis or fixed angle grammar changes coverage or hold timing across the exchange, with a same-trigger boundary; otherwise they are rejected as descriptive coverage patterns.

reasons: A long clean single can drift in framing or screen direction.
The delayed receiver cut must match the owner endpoint without inventing overlap.
A sustained subtle progression can flatten, loop, or add unsupported business.

applicable_when: One visible performance progression, rather than a concurrent task state, owns the interval.
runtime_rule_specs.blocking: Keep the performance owner readable without inventing business; retain other participants off the critical visual axis until the owner interval completes.
runtime_rule_specs.continuity: Preserve entry posture, gaze direction, screen side, and the visible endpoint used by the delayed receiver cut.

counterexample.notes: The same principal-performance trigger includes required concurrent material and other-body task state, so shared work coverage and selective checks replace the clean owner hold.

runtime_rule_specs.coverage: Register the relation first, then use one clean owner single and a later receiver or relation check.
runtime_rule_specs.director_decision: Reduce relation anchors progressively, give the performance owner a clean sustained single, and postpone receiver coverage until the owner interval completes.
runtime_rule_specs.edit_logic: Enter after relation registration and cut away after the principal visible progression reaches its locked endpoint.
failure_modes: Routine reaction cutting interrupts the locked progression.
A clean single hides a simultaneous state that the story requires the audience to track.

fallback.camera: Use two shorter project-original locked singles on the same screen side, separated only at a verified performance endpoint.
fallback.continuity: Return to a neutral project-original two-person relation frame before the delayed receiver shot.
fallback.performance: Split the progression into two explicit project-original posture or gaze states instead of asking for one continuous subtle arc.

runtime_rule_specs.name: Hold the principal visible performance after relation registration
not_applicable_when: A simultaneous action, object, safety, or receiver state must remain visible.
runtime_rule_specs.pacing: Let the owner interval run without routine reaction cutting; shorten only when a locked concurrent state appears.
required_story_facts: The participant relation has already been visibly established.
One project-original performance progression must remain continuously readable.
No simultaneous action, object, safety, or receiver state is locked for the owner interval.

supporting_relations.notes: A two-person relation frame precedes a long clean owner single, followed by relation coverage only after the visible owner interval.

runtime_rule_specs.trigger: After the relation is registered, one uninterrupted visible performance progression is the principal locked fact and no concurrent action state must remain visible.

reasons: Continuous reframing across a zone change can distort scale or axis.
The mover, counterpart, and destination zone can drift across coverage.
Body-level and route endpoints can be underspecified or mistimed.

applicable_when: The spatial change and its two-person endpoint both occur in continuous present time.
runtime_rule_specs.blocking: Let the mover cross the project-original zone while the relation anchor remains readable; do not hide the new relation behind an isolated insert.
runtime_rule_specs.continuity: Preserve screen side, route direction, source zone, destination zone, and the counterpart's relation anchor.

counterexample.notes: The second occupancy change occurs after the counterpart is absent, so a fixed room anchor makes another relation reset unnecessary.

runtime_rule_specs.coverage: Use a shared transition or relation-reset frame that contains the mover, counterpart, and changed endpoint.
runtime_rule_specs.director_decision: Show the spatial change or its endpoint in shared or continuously reframed relation coverage before returning to isolated coverage.
runtime_rule_specs.edit_logic: Place the return to isolated coverage after the relation endpoint is visible, not during the unregistered spatial change.
failure_modes: Returning to singles before the changed relation is visible.
Adding a relation reset after the counterpart has left and the fixed room anchor already explains the movement.

fallback.camera: Use a locked project-original wide that contains source and destination zones instead of a moving reset.
fallback.continuity: Insert a neutral project-original room map showing both screen sides and the destination zone before resuming singles.
fallback.performance: Split the movement into a clear start pose and destination pose with one simple crossing action.

runtime_rule_specs.name: Re-establish the relation after a material spatial change
not_applicable_when: The counterpart is already absent and the remaining movement is readable against a fixed room anchor.
runtime_rule_specs.pacing: Hold the reset until the changed level, zone, or distance reads, then resume singles.
required_story_facts: A participant changes level, zone, or distance enough to invalidate the prior relation frame.
The changed relation to a present counterpart remains story-critical.

supporting_relations.notes: A shared seated-to-standing change is followed by standing coverage and a renewed shared relation.

runtime_rule_specs.trigger: A body-level, zone, or distance change invalidates the prior relation geometry while the counterpart relation remains a locked visible fact.

reasons: A shared approach can produce scale, axis, or collision drift.
Start and end distances, body levels, and no-contact state must remain consistent.
Timing the stop and mutual awareness without added contact is delicate.

applicable_when: The continuous path, not merely the terminal spacing, carries required relation information.
runtime_rule_specs.blocking: Use a project-original route with a fixed relation anchor and a visible stop; do not add contact or surface imitation.
runtime_rule_specs.continuity: Preserve axis, start distance, route direction, end distance, level, and the no-contact boundary when locked.

counterexample.notes: The relation distance changes across editorial time ellipsis, so only the terminal shared geometry should be shown; a continuous approach would invent an event.

runtime_rule_specs.coverage: Begin with readable two-person geometry, carry the approach or level change in shared coverage, then hold the endpoint.
runtime_rule_specs.director_decision: Register the initial zones, show the change in shared or continuous relation coverage, and hold the shared endpoint before isolating faces.
runtime_rule_specs.edit_logic: Avoid cutting over the critical relation transition; cut after the endpoint reads or use one continuous shared shot.
failure_modes: Tight coverage hides the relation-change path.
A continuous approach is fabricated for an elliptical change.
Unspecified contact is added at the endpoint.

fallback.camera: Use a locked project-original shared wide with marked start and end positions instead of a moving camera.
fallback.continuity: Render separate project-original start and endpoint plates and cut only after each geometry is readable.
fallback.performance: Use one simple approach and a clear stop, with no contact unless the project-original facts require it.

runtime_rule_specs.name: Show a continuous relation change and hold its shared endpoint
not_applicable_when: The distance change occurs across time ellipsis or only the terminal geometry is story-critical.
runtime_rule_specs.pacing: Delay tight isolated coverage until the continuous distance change and endpoint have both registered.
required_story_facts: The project-original relation distance or body level changes in continuous present time.
The transition path and two-person endpoint must both be visible.
Contact is not inferred unless separately locked.

supporting_relations.notes: A visible level change resolves into shared two-person proximity coverage and a held endpoint.

runtime_rule_specs.trigger: A relationship-relevant distance or level change happens in continuous present time and both its path and shared endpoint are locked visible facts.

reasons: Scale can drift between the field and selected detail.
Referents can change count, shape, or orientation across cuts.
Performance requirements are limited to clear handling.

applicable_when: The audience must compare visible referents before an isolated relation or handling detail becomes readable.
runtime_rule_specs.blocking: Keep the visible referents simultaneously readable long enough to establish their relation; do not copy source props.
runtime_rule_specs.continuity: Preserve referent count, relative scale, orientation, and the relation used by the next action.

counterexample.notes: A single item state is readable without a simultaneous comparative field; forcing a comparison would add unsupported alternatives.

runtime_rule_specs.coverage: Use a field view containing all relevant referents, then move to the relation or handling detail without claiming an unseen selection.
runtime_rule_specs.director_decision: Establish the full comparison field and common visual relation before isolating the relation used by the next action.
runtime_rule_specs.edit_logic: Cut from the established comparison field to the relevant relation, not from an unexplained isolated insert.
failure_modes: An isolated item appears before the comparison condition is readable.
Generated alternatives drift or become indistinguishable.

fallback.camera: Use a locked project-original overhead comparison plate.
fallback.continuity: Label project-original referent positions in the IR and preserve them across Shots.
fallback.performance: Use one simple point-and-place action after the field is established.

runtime_rule_specs.name: Register the comparative field before isolating the relevant relation
not_applicable_when: Only one item state matters and no comparative field is required.
runtime_rule_specs.pacing: Hold the comparison field until the relation reads, then move into the next project-original action.
required_story_facts: At least two project-original referents are simultaneously visible.
Their visible relation must be understood before the next action or detail.

supporting_relations.notes: A visible record field precedes a moving relation between one record and a live spatial anchor; no record meaning or final selection is claimed.

runtime_rule_specs.trigger: Two or more project-original referents must be read together before one visible relation can guide the next action.
